newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Di Rupo seen victim of fight between courts and MPs.
newsitem.headline: Di Rupo seen victim of fight between courts and MPs.

text.p: Deputy Prime Minister Elio di Rupo, under investigation over sex allegations, has been caught up in a struggle between Belgium's courts and the world of politics, analysts and media said.

Several newspapers said on Friday the sole witness who alleged Di Rupo had sex with under-age boys was not credible and suggested the judiciary had attacked Di Rupo to deflect the government from reforming the justice system.

That system has been widely criticised for its handling of a child murder scandal centring around Marc Dutroux, the main suspect in a paedophile ring which has claimed the lives of at least four girls.

"It is striking that as soon as the political authorities attack the Brussels court about (the handling of) the Dutroux case, the court strikes back at the world of politics," RUG University sociology professor John Vincke told Reuters.
The government is preparing a review of the justice system, against the background of the 100-day old murder scandal.

"The judiciary feels threatened and fears that the political world will proceed to a drastic reform of the justice system. And the best defence...is counter-attack," said De Standaard in an editorial.
On Thursday, Le Soir quoted a Belgian parliament member as saying: "Are (the courts) trying to make the government fall so the Dutroux commission cannot go all the way ?"
A parliamentary commission is also investigating accusations by the families of the victims that the police and justice system made mistakes in the Dutroux investigation.

Government spokeswoman Moniek Delvou declined comment, but referred to a speech by Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene in parliament on Thursday, in which he lashed out at the court's approach of the Di Rupo investigation in which "the authenticity of certain facts was not deemed worth checking."

On Monday, the Brussels prosecutor-general gave the Belgian parliament a report in which Olivier Trusgnach, a 22-year old Belgian homosexual, is reported as saying that he had been present at parties in which Di Rupo had sex with under-age boys.
Trusgnach is reported to have said he himself was 15 at the time of the parties, which he said happened around 1989-90.

Based on this report, the Belgian parliament on Thursday asked the Cour de Cassation, Belgium's highest court, to further investigate the allegations against Di Rupo and make a new report to parliament by December 9 at the latest.
Di Rupo, a discreet homosexual, has denied the allegations.
Several papers quoted parliament members talking about the "unbearable lightness" of the prosecutor's report.
Trusgnach is currently in jail in Hasselt, northeastern Belgium, for theft.
Three newspaper quoted Trusgnach's mother (who visited him in jail) as saying he could not possibly have met Di Rupo at 15.

"It is simply impossible that my son would have had contact with (Di Rupo) at age 15. Olivier hardly ever left the house and was still very immature at that age," she told Het Belang van Limburg, adding the boy only started going out when he was 17.
She also said her son and had "a rich imagination".
The legal age of consent in Belgium is 16.
